title: Average the scores
description: Find the average of two riddle scores, decimals and all.

tasks.title: Two kinds of numbers
tasks.body: Python has two kinds of numbers. An int is a whole number, like 7 or -3. A float has a decimal point, like 2.5 or 7.0. Dividing with / always gives a float, even when the answer is whole: 6 / 3 is 2.0.
tasks.detail: When a calculation mixes an int and a float, the answer is a float: 2 + 0.5 is 2.5. int() cuts off the decimal part without rounding, so int(3.9) is 3 and int(-2.5) is -2. A few decimals print oddly, like 0.1 + 0.2 showing 0.30000000000000004. That comes from how computers store decimals, not from a mistake in your code.

tasks.code:
# How long the walk to the market takes
distance = 9
speed = 2
hours = distance / speed
print(hours)
# The whole hours, with the decimal part cut off
print(int(hours))
# / gives a float even when the answer is whole
print(8 / 2)
tasks.note: hours holds the float 4.5. int() cuts off the .5 and gives the int 4. The last line shows 4.0, not 4, because / always gives a float.

tasks.question: What would print(int(7.9)) display?
tasks.why: int() cuts off everything after the decimal point; it does not round up. So int(7.9) is 7, even though 7.9 is close to 8.

tasks.prompt: Change distance to 10. Before you run, predict the first line: will it still have a decimal point? Then change the last line to print(8 // 2), predict again, and compare the two answers.

After two riddles, the hero has two scores. A wrong answer can make a score negative. The starter asks for both scores. Print two lines: first the average of the two scores, then the same average with its decimal part cut off by int(). Print just the two numbers.
tasks.starter:
# These two lines ask for whole-number scores (lesson 3 explains how)
first = int(input("First score? "))
second = int(input("Second score? "))
# Work out the average, then print it and its whole part
hints: The average of two scores is their total divided by 2. You print it twice: once as it is, and once with its decimal part cut off.
Look at the order Python works in: it divides before it adds. Check that your whole total gets divided, not only the second score.
With other names: total = low + high adds first, and then total / 2 halves it. For your second line, think about which function cuts off the decimal part.

error_hints.text: Use the names from the starter, first and second, and give your average a name before you print it.
Print each number on its own, like print(total). Joining a number to text with + needs str(), and this check wants only the numbers.
The average of 7 and 8 is 7.5. If your first line says 11.0, Python divided only the second score: put the addition inside parentheses.
With -3 and 2, the average is -0.5. int() cuts off the decimal part, so the second line is 0. The // operator rounds down instead, which gives -1 for negative numbers.
Your program needs to work for any two scores. Use first and second in the calculation, not numbers typed into the code.

similar_example.note: Halfway between a morning temperature of 4 and an evening of 9 is 6.5. Your challenge reads its two numbers from the replies, and also prints the whole part.

other_ways.code:
first = int(input("First score? "))
second = int(input("Second score? "))
total = first + second
print(total / 2)
print(int(total / 2))
other_ways.note: Keep the total in its own variable first.

other_ways.code:
first = int(input("First score? "))
second = int(input("Second score? "))
average = (first + second) * 0.5
print(average)
print(int(average))
other_ways.note: Multiplying by 0.5 halves a number too, and the answer is also a float.
